lines.text: You put on headphones, press one button, and the airplane engine just disappears. How do you delete a sound?
Sound is a wave. Air squeezed and stretched, squeezed and stretched, hundreds of times a second.
Tiny microphones on the outside of the headphones listen to that noise, all the time.
Then a chip builds the exact opposite wave. Where the noise squeezes, it stretches. Where it stretches, it squeezes.
Play both at once, and they cancel out. Squeeze plus stretch equals, nothing. Silence.
And it has to keep up, adjusting thousands of times every second, because the noise never stops changing.
It works best on steady rumbles, like engines and air conditioners. Sudden sounds, like a voice or a clap, are harder.
That's why the ear cushions matter too. They physically block the high-pitched sounds the chip can't catch.
And transparency mode? It flips the trick around, and plays the outside world back into your ears.
Want to cancel the noise in your team's files? Orbi Work: every file wired to a task, every task with clear steps. No endless chat.
orbitransfer.com, slash work. Now you know!
